v.story-team.intro.1.text: Vowel Team Harbor is busy with boats, and its vowels travel in pairs.

v.story-team.intro.2.text: Two vowels side by side can work as a team, and together they make one new sound.

v.story-team.intro.3.text: Find the torn pages on the docks, and listen for the sound each team makes.

v.story-team.team-ai-ay.1.text: A lady waves from the bay, and the words on her sail hold ai and ay.

v.story-team.team-ai-ay.2.text: When ai or ay appears, the pair says the long a sound, so read the pair together.

v.story-team.team-ee-ea.1.text: Seaweed floats near the pier, and its name holds a pair of vowels that say long e.

v.story-team.team-ee-ea.2.text: Ee and ea often say the long e sound, so read the pair as one clear note.

v.story-team.team-oa-igh.1.text: A raincoat hangs on the pier, and its name holds oa, which says long o.

v.story-team.team-oa-igh.2.text: Igh and ie both say the long i sound, like a kite flying high over the harbor.

v.story-team.team-oo-ew.1.text: A balloon floats over the harbor, and its name has two o's that sing the long oo sound.

v.story-team.team-oo-ew.2.text: Ew and ue can say the oo sound too, so try one sound, then listen and try again.

v.story-team.team-au-oi.1.text: A hawk circles the boat, and the aw in its name makes a bold sound.

v.story-team.team-au-oi.2.text: Oi and oy share one sound, like a coin dropping onto the deck.

v.story-team.team-ou-ow.1.text: A brown owl sits on a rainbow over the harbor, and both brown and owl use ow.

v.story-team.team-ou-ow.2.text: Ou and ow can say the ow sound in a cloud, or the long o sound in a bowl.

v.story-team.team-mix.1.text: A harbor breakfast table holds many team words, and each pair has its own sound.

v.story-team.team-mix.2.text: Read each pair of vowels carefully, check which sound fits, and the whole table comes alive.

v.story-team.finale.1.text: The harbor boats are sailing again, and the team pages are back in the Great Word Book.

v.story-team.finale.2.text: The Keeper says, 'Next are the mountains, where an r changes the vowel right before it.'
